standard.title: Plan, create and publish texts
standard.description: plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal imaginative, informative and persuasive texts, using visual features, relevant linked ideas, complex sentences, appropriate tense, synonyms and antonyms, correct spelling of multisyllabic words and simple punctuation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts using visual features, paragraphs and topic vocabulary (AC9E3LY06). They have not yet planned and created texts using complex sentences, linked ideas, synonyms/antonyms, multisyllabic word spelling and simple punctuation across all three text types.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts across three text types — imaginative, informative and persuasive — using complex sentences, linked ideas, appropriate tense, precise vocabulary and correct spelling and punctuation.

nodes.label: Planning — structure and content
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a written or multimodal text by selecting appropriate structure, grouping ideas into logical sections and deciding on key vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a plan for a text that identifies the text type structure, groups ideas into at least two sections and notes key vocabulary.
nodes.typical_width: Plan texts across all three text types — imaginative, informative and persuasive — selecting appropriate structure for each, organising ideas into logical paragraph groups and planning vocabulary including synonyms and precise terms.
wider: Use digital planning tools (mind-mapping, outline software) to organise and restructure ideas before writing, comparing the outcome with a handwritten plan
Plan a multimodal text, considering how visual and verbal elements will work together at each stage of the text
nodes.hinge_reason: Creating with complex sentences and linked ideas in N2 requires a planned text structure — without a plan, students cannot make or evaluate deliberate organisational choices when drafting.

response_modes.reason: Planning across three text types requires explicit reasoning about how structure serves purpose — selecting between narrative, report and argument structures is not intuitive at Year 4 without a scaffolded decision process.

success_criteria: Plan includes identified text type structure with at least two sections
Plan includes key vocabulary noted before writing begins

nodes.label: Creating — complex sentences and linked ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create texts using complex sentences and text connectives to link ideas coherently within and across paragraphs.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text that includes at least two complex sentences and one text connective linking ideas between sentences.
nodes.typical_width: Create texts using a range of complex sentences (with temporal, causal and conditional subordination) and text connectives to link ideas coherently within and across paragraphs, with appropriate tense for text type.
wider: Create texts in two different text types on the same topic and compare how sentence structure and connective choices change to suit each purpose
Create a multimodal informative text that integrates verbal and visual elements to communicate linked ideas
nodes.hinge_reason: Editing in N3 requires a created text with vocabulary, spelling and punctuation choices to review — N3 cannot proceed without the artefact N2 produces.

response_modes.reason: Creating a cohesive text integrates knowledge from across Language — complex sentences, text connectives, tense, vocabulary — into a coordinated writing performance. This is the integration node for the whole writing system.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creating across three text types with complex sentences and linked ideas is genuinely wide — the range of purposes, structures and audiences produces rich variation in craft choices.
success_criteria: Text includes at least one complex sentence with a named subordinating conjunction
Text includes at least one text connective linking ideas between sentences
Tense is appropriate and consistent for the text type

nodes.label: Editing — vocabulary, spelling and punctuation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit their texts to improve vocabulary choices (synonyms, precise terms), correct multisyllabic spelling and ensure consistent punctuation.
nodes.minimum_width: Edit a piece of writing by changing at least one word to a more precise synonym and checking the spelling of at least two multisyllabic words.
nodes.typical_width: Edit texts systematically for vocabulary precision (selecting synonyms, replacing vague words), correct spelling of multisyllabic words and consistent simple punctuation — reviewing each dimension as a separate editing pass.
wider: Develop a personal editing checklist based on recurring errors and apply it to successive drafts across different text types
Compare first draft and edited version, annotating specific changes and explaining the reason for each improvement

response_modes.reason: Editing for vocabulary, spelling and punctuation requires habitual checking — students who understand what to look for still need practice making systematic review automatic rather than selective.

success_criteria: Has changed at least one word to a more precise or varied synonym
Has corrected at least one multisyllabic word spelling
Punctuation is consistent throughout the text
